MENU_QUICK_DESC: Any two teams, any venue. Play now.
MENU_SEASON_DESC: A full league season in Malaysia, Thailand or Indonesia.
MENU_CUP_DESC: The world's best nations, Asia's and Southeast Asia's.
EVENT_NOTE_REGU: Three a side: the tekong serves, the feeder sets, the striker spikes.
EVENT_NOTE_TEAM: Three regu matches in a row, no player twice. First to win two takes the tie.
EVENT_NOTE_QUADRANT: Four a side, two strikers. Served from behind the back line.
EVENT_NOTE_DOUBLES: Two a side: a server and a striker cover the whole court.
DIFF_EASY_DESC: Wide timing, forgiving touches, opponents who make mistakes.
DIFF_NORMAL_DESC: A fair game: good timing wins rallies.
DIFF_PRO_DESC: Tight timing and sharp opponents who read your spikes.
DIFF_LEGEND_DESC: World-class opponents. Every touch must be on time.
VENUE_NATIONAL_DESC: Indoors, 3,000 seats, LED boards: the home of the national team.
VENUE_MALL_DESC: A court in a shopping mall, fans on every floor, as the great invitational tournaments are played.
VENUE_PROVINCIAL_DESC: A wooden floor, a few rows of seats and fans turning overhead.
VENUE_PARK_DESC: An evening game under the floodlights.
VENUE_BEACH_DESC: Beach takraw on the sand at sunset.
LEAGUE_NOTE_MY: Malaysia. Twelve clubs in the Premier Division play seven Grand Prix, each a tournament: groups of three, quarter-finals, semi-finals, the final. Points for every finish; the last two go down to Division 1.
LEAGUE_NOTE_TH: Thailand. Eight provincial clubs, home and away. Every fixture is a tie of two regus: 2 points for winning both, 1 for one each. Top of the table wins.
LEAGUE_NOTE_ID: Indonesia, men's and women's. Five regions play a round robin; the top two of each go to the national finals in Jakarta.
ABANDON_SEASON_Q: Abandon this season? It cannot be undone.
CUP_WORLD_DESC: The strongest nations in the Mall Atrium. Both losing semi-finalists take bronze.
CUP_ROYAL_DESC: A yearly invitational tournament, played on a court in a shopping mall.
CUP_ASIA_DESC: Asia's nations in the National Arena.
CUP_SEA_DESC: The region's great rivalries, in a provincial gym.
OUT_OF_CUP: Your tournament is over. See how it ends?
FAULT_FOOT: Fault: the server's foot left the circle
ASSIST_OFF_NOTE: You run your player to every ball with the joystick. Every touch is yours to time.
ASSIST_RUN_NOTE: You run to the ball for the first touch; your setter and striker run to theirs. You time every touch.
ASSIST_FULL_NOTE: Your players run to the ball themselves. You still time every touch, and aim.
GFX_NOTE: Low keeps budget phones smooth; the game picks it for you on phones that need it.
FPS_NOTE_SAVER: About {n} frames a second: longer battery, a cooler phone.
FPS_NOTE_SMOOTH: {n} frames a second on your {hz} Hz screen.
FPS_NOTE_MAX: As many frames as your {hz} Hz screen shows.
PRIV_SUMMARY: Sepak Takraw Unleashed collects no personal data. There is no account, no sign-in, no server, no analytics, no advertising and no in-app purchases. The game has no permission to use the internet, so it cannot send anything anywhere.
PRIV_KEEP: Your settings, the season or tournament you are playing and your records. They are kept in the game's own storage on your phone, are never sent anywhere, and are deleted when you uninstall the game.
PRIV_PERM: Only vibration, to buzz the phone when your player touches the ball (you can turn it off in {settings}). The game does not use your location, camera, microphone, contacts or files.
PRIV_CHILD: The game collects no information from anyone, children included.
PRIV_CHANGE: If this ever changes, an update of the game will say so here first, with a new date.
HELP_PLAY: Nothing is played for you. Your player is lit in gold: run him with the joystick to the gold mark on the floor, and press as the ring closing on the ball meets the gold circle. Too early, too late or too far away, and he misses it.
HELP_SERVE: Press {serve} as the thrown ball drops to your foot: on time, the serve goes over hard and flat. {horse} is the fast sole serve. Aim with the joystick.
HELP_ATTACK: Your feeder sets and your striker spikes: push the joystick to aim, and {feint} drops the ball over the block. When they set their striker, {block} appears: slide along the net and jump as he hits.
HELP_SLOW: {settings} > {speed} > {slow}, and {assist} > {full}: your players run to the ball themselves and you time the touches.
HELP_PHONE: {settings} > {graphics} > {low}, and {fps} > {saver}. Budget phones start on {low} by themselves.
HELP_WORDS: Buttons hard to reach? {settings} > {size}, and {left} to swap their sides. Words wrong in your language? Tell us which screen and what it says.
HELP_CONTACT: Email {email} with your phone's model and what happened. We read everything.
LICENCES_INTRO: What the game is made with, and under what licences.
RULES_COURT_TEXT: 13.40 m by 6.10 m, a badminton doubles court. The net is 1.52 m high for men and 1.42 m for women. A quarter circle by the net on each side, and a service circle 2.45 m from each back line.
RULES_PLAYERS_TEXT: Three players: the tekong, who serves from the back; the feeder, who sets; and the striker, who spikes. Quadrant is four a side, doubles two.
RULES_SERVE_TEXT: An inside player throws the ball to the tekong, who kicks it over with one foot in the service circle. Both inside players must stand in their quarter circles until it is kicked. The serve passes to the other side after every point.
RULES_TOUCHES_TEXT: Feet, knees, chest and head: never the hands or arms. Three touches a side at most, and one player may make all three.
RULES_SCORE_TEXT: Every rally wins a point. Sets go to 15; from 14 all a set must be won by two, up to 17. Best of three sets. Ends change after each set, and at 8 in the third.
RULES_FAULTS_TEXT: Touching the net, the ball on a hand or arm, a fourth touch, the ball under the net or outside the boundary tape, the server's standing foot leaving the circle.
RULES_CHALLENGE_TEXT: One challenge a side a set on a line call. Win it and you keep it.
CTRL_TIMING_TEXT: Nothing is played for you: your player kicks only when you press. A ring closes on the ball: press as it meets the gold circle. Too early, too late or too far from the ball, and he misses it.
CTRL_SERVE_TEXT: Press Serve as the thrown ball drops to your foot, or Horse kick for the fast sole serve over the shoulder. Timed well, the serve goes over hard and flat. Aim with the joystick. Miss it and it is a fault.
CTRL_PASS_TEXT: Get under the ball and press Kick (Dig against a spike) as the ring closes. A good first touch reaches your feeder by the net.
CTRL_SET_TEXT: Set lofts it high for a roll spike; Quick set is lower and faster; Attack surprises them with a second-touch kill.
CTRL_SPIKE_TEXT: Spike plays your striker's signature spike. Push the joystick to aim; Feint drops it softly over the block.
CTRL_BLOCK_TEXT: When they set their striker, Block appears: slide along the net with the joystick, and jump as he hits.
CTRL_ASSIST_TEXT: Standard: you run for the first touch; your setter and striker run to theirs. Full: they all run for you. Off: you run for every touch. You always time the touch yourself.
CTRL_KEYS_TEXT: WASD or arrows to aim and move, Space for the first button, J and K for the others.
MOVE_SILA_TEXT: The inside-of-the-foot kick: the basic receive and set.
MOVE_KUDA_TEXT: The instep kick, stretched out for low balls and digs.
MOVE_HORSE_TEXT: The sunback serve: turned away from the net, the sole whips the ball over the shoulder.
MOVE_ROLL_TEXT: The full somersault, the foot driving the ball down over the shoulder at up to 130 km/h. Thailand's trademark.
MOVE_SUNBACK_TEXT: A jumping horse kick, side-on, the legs scissoring: the Malaysian kalih.
MOVE_TAPAK_TEXT: The tapak: the sole stamps the ball down over the net.
MOVE_HEADER_TEXT: To receive, to set, or to spike from the net.
MOVE_FEINT_TEXT: A soft touch just over the block when they expect the spike.
MOVE_BLOCK_TEXT: A jump at the net, legs up, to stop the spike coming through.
RECORDS_BEST_KILLS: Most kills in a match: {n}, {p} against {t}
RECORDS_BEST_BLOCKS: Most blocks in a match: {n}, {p} against {t}
RECORDS_BEST_ACES: Most aces in a match: {n}, {p} against {t}
RECORDS_NONE: No titles yet. Go and win one!
SPEED_NOTE: How fast a match runs. Slow gives you time to read the ball and run to it; Real is takraw at full speed.
CTRL_MOVE_TEXT: The player lit in gold is yours. Run him with the joystick to the gold mark on the floor: it turns green when he is close enough. Let go near it and he steps onto it.
STL_POINTS_NOTE: Each Grand Prix: 32 points to the winner, 28 the runner-up, 24 third, 21 fourth, 15 a quarter-finalist, 8 a win in the group. The most points win the league; the last two go down.
TIE_TWO_REGUS: A tie of two regus, and you play both: 2 points for winning both, 1 for one each.
YOU_RELEGATED: Your club goes down to Division 1. Win your way back next season.
YOU_STAY_DIV1: Your club stays in Division 1. Reach the final to go up.
ABOUT_DISCLAIMER: Sepak Takraw Unleashed is an independent game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by any sepak takraw federation, league, club or player. The clubs' nicknames are invented and the players are fictional; the countries, places and rules are real.
GFX_LOWERED: Graphics lowered to keep the game smooth (Settings).
GFX_AUTO_PICK: Auto: {level} on this phone, picked from its chip and memory.
GFX_NEXT_MATCH: In a match, the venue and the crowd change from the next match.
PLAY_AS_TEAM_NOTE: Every touch on your side is yours, whoever the ball comes to.
PLAY_AS_ONE_NOTE: Only that player's touches are yours (the white ring); your team-mates play theirs. In doubles, Feeder is the striker.
